source_question: Let $b \geq 2$ be an integer. Call a positive integer $n$ $b\textit{-eautiful}$ if it has exactly two digits when expressed in base $b$ , and these two digits sum to $\sqrt{n}$ . For example, $81$ is $13$ -eautiful because $81=\underline{6}$ $\underline{3}_{13}$ and $6+3=\sqrt{81}$ . Find the least integer $b\geq 2$ for which there are more than ten $b$ -eautiful integers.
